Rubén Darío was a Nicaraguan poet, the leader of modernismo, the movement that renewed poetry in the Spanish language around 1900. He is called the prince of Castilian letters.

Raised in León, he was a famous child poet. His book Azul, published in Chile in 1888, brought the music and imagery of French poetry into Spanish verse. He worked as a journalist and diplomat in Buenos Aires, Madrid and Paris, and his later books, such as Songs of Life and Hope (1905), influenced writers across Spain and the Americas.

In his poem To Roosevelt he warned the United States against swallowing Spanish America, a theme of his age of banana republics and the occupations that followed. He died in León. He is the national poet of Nicaragua, and the first great Latin American writer read in Spain, the forerunner of Neruda.
